TinyML Edge Debugging

This sample demonstrates how to use the TinyML library to implement serial communication between the RTL87x2G and a host (PC). It supports the host sending model files and input data to the device through a custom UART protocol, and the device completes the TFLite inference and reports the result back to the host.

In this sample, the device receives data packets sent by the host through the UART interface. After protocol parsing, it sequentially performs model loading, parameter configuration, and inference, and then sends the inference result, memory usage, inference time, and other information back to the host through response packets.

The system architecture is shown in the figure below. The overall architecture is divided into two parts: the PC host and the Edge Device, which communicate bidirectionally through the UART interface.

The PC host consists of the following three modules:

  • EdgeAI and UART Model: Manages models and communicates with the Edge Device via the UART protocol for command interaction and data transfer.

  • Model Export: Exports the trained TFLite model as a C array for direct integration into the embedded project.

  • Emulated Inference: Performs local model inference on the PC for quick validation without requiring a physical device.

The Edge Device consists of the following components:

  • UART Protocol Driver: Implements the custom UART communication protocol, handling packet transmission, reception, parsing, and assembly.

  • TFLite Model Buffer/Model Data Buffer: Receives, manages, and stores the model file and inference input data sent from the PC host.

  • Inference Runtime: The TFLite-based inference engine that loads the model data sent from the PC and executes the actual inference on the device.

The host interface is shown below:

The meaning of each field and button on the host interface is described below:

Host Interface Description

Field/Button

Description

Model

Selects the TFLite model file (.tflite) to deploy to the device.

Data

Selects the input data file (.bin) used for inference.

Local Model Analysis

Local emulated inference: replicates the inference flow on the PC without a device, for quickly validating model correctness.

Parameter Export

Model export: exports the TFLite model as a C array (generates model_tflite.cpp) for direct integration into the embedded project.

Model Inference

On-device inference: sends the selected model and data to the device to run TFLite inference, then reports and displays the result, latency, and memory usage.

Open Port/Close Port

Opens or closes the serial connection.

COM Port

Selects the serial port connected to the device (e.g. COM4).

Baud Rate

Sets the serial communication baud rate; must match the device (default 115200).

Log Area

Shows the command interaction between the host and the device, the inference results, and error messages.

Wiring

The device communicates with the host through UART. The interface pins are shown in the table below:

UART Interface Pins

Pin Name

PIN

Meaning

UART_TX

P3_0

Transmit data

UART_RX

P3_1

Receive data

GND

GND

Reference ground

Communication parameters: baud rate 115200, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit, no parity.

Building and Downloading

The project path of this sample is as follows:

Project file: samples\tinyml\tinyml_edge\proj\rtl87x2g\mdk

Project file: samples\tinyml\tinyml_edge\proj\rtl87x2g\gcc

Follow the steps below to build and run this sample:

  1. Open the project file.

  2. To build the target, follow the steps listed on the Generating App Image in Quick Start.

  3. After a successful build, the app bin app_MP_xxx.bin is generated under mdk\bin or gcc\bin.

  4. To download the app bin into the EVB, follow the steps listed on the MP Tool Download in Quick Start.

  5. Connect P3_0 (TX) and P3_1 (RX) of the EVB to the host serial port through a USB-UART adapter.

  6. Press the reset button to start running.

Test Verification

  1. Open the host software TinyML_Host, select the model file (.tflite) and input data file (.bin) to test, and click the Model Inference button. The host automatically completes the following full inference process.

  2. An example of the host inference log is shown below. The complete process is: get device name → query memory → load model → load data → configure parameters → download file → trigger inference → receive result.

    IO_MSG_UART_RX_DONE

Protocol Description

The UART data packet format is as follows:

Data Packet Frame Format

Field

Length

Description

Header

2 bytes

Fixed to 0xAA 0xBB

Data Length

2 bytes

Length of the valid data area

Sequence Number

2 bytes

Packet sequence number, used for ACK matching and retransmission

Command

1 byte

Command type, see the table below

Data Area

N bytes

Payload attached to the command

CRC

2 bytes

Data checksum

Footer

1 byte

Fixed to 0xCC

The supported commands are as follows:

Command Definitions

Command Name

Command

Description

GET_DEVICE_NAME

0x40

Get device name

GET_MEM_SIZE

0x41

Get available memory size

LOAD_MODEL

0x42

Load TFLite model file

LOAD_DATA

0x43

Load inference input data

CONFIG_PARAM

0x44

Configure inference parameters

MODEL_INFER

0x45

Perform inference

DOWNLOAD_MODEL_FILE

0x46

Download model file to device

DOWNLOAD_DATA_FILE

0x47

Download data file to device

The event codes actively reported by the device are as follows:

Event Report Code Definitions

Event Name

Event Code

Description

REPORT_ARENA_SIZE

0x50

Report Tensor Arena memory usage

REPORT_INFER_CYCLES

0x51

Report inference time (CPU cycles)

REPORT_OPS_LIST

0x52

Report model operator list

REPORT_QUANT_PARAMS

0x53

Report quantization parameters

REPORT_INFER_RESULT

0x55

Report inference result

REPORT_PROFILER

0x56

Report per-operator Profiler performance data

Initialization

  1. Set the CPU operating frequency to 125 MHz and initialize the DWT cycle counter.

  2. Call uart_init to initialize UART (P3_0 TX/P3_1 RX, baud rate 115200).

  3. Create the IO message queue (capacity 0x30 messages) to receive event messages issued by the UART interrupt callback.

  4. Create a timeout timer (8000 ms) to handle ACK response timeout.

    uart_init();
os_msg_queue_create(&tinyml_queue_handle, "TSQ",
                    MAX_NUMBER_OF_IO_MESSAGE, sizeof(T_IO_MSG));
os_timer_create(&xUartTimeoutTimerHandle, "timeout Timer",
                1, 8000, false, ts_timer_cb);

Functional Implementation

  1. The main task loop blocks waiting on the IO message queue. When UART reception completes (IO_MSG_UART_RX_DONE), it takes the received raw bytes from the global data linked list and calls uart_rx_data_parse for protocol parsing.

  2. After protocol parsing succeeds (IO_MSG_UART_DATA_PARSER_SUCCESS), it executes the corresponding command (load model, load data, perform inference, etc.) and sends the response packet back to the host through uart_send_with_ack, with support for timeout retransmission.

  3. When protocol parsing fails (IO_MSG_UART_DATA_PARSER_FAILED), a retransmission request is triggered.

    if (event.subtype == IO_MSG_UART_RX_DONE)
{
    /* uart rx data parse */
}
else if (event.subtype == IO_MSG_UART_DATA_PARSER_SUCCESS)
{
    /* execute command and reply */
}
else if (event.subtype == IO_MSG_UART_DATA_PARSER_FAILED)
{
    /* trigger retransmission */
}

  4. The host writes the model file and input data into the device buffer (model_buf/data_buf) through UART_CMD_CONFIG_PARAM (0x44) and the file download commands. After receiving UART_CMD_MODEL_INFER (0x45), it calls MinimalInferenceWithTime to complete the inference: registers the model and the memory allocation hooks, tries different Arena sizes (192 KB→128 KB→96 KB) to initialize the inference engine, calls ts_realtek_invoke to perform inference, and finally sends the inference result, memory usage, operator information, and other data back to the host through event packets.
